intro: Section 23.6 covers biofeedback: its theory, the instruments and body signals it uses, and the relaxation methods that go with it (Table 23-8), autogenic training (Table 23-9), applied tension and applied relaxation (Table 23-10), with indications and results. A dashed box adds a recent blinded-outcome meta-analysis of neurofeedback for ADHD.
objectives: Define biofeedback and explain the learning theory behind it.
Name the instruments and physiologic signals used in biofeedback.
Compare the main relaxation methods (Table 23-8) and describe autogenic training (Table 23-9).
Explain applied tension and when it is used instead of relaxation.
Outline the steps of applied relaxation (Table 23-10) and the reported results.
